item.title: Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championships to be held this month in Suva
item.description: Speaking to fijivillage news, Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Vice-President, Josua Qalo says Wainibuka Secondary School announced itself as one of the teams to watch after winning the Under-15 title in the Eastern Rally. He says Vunimono High School also continued its rise by claiming the Under-17 title, while retaining the boys' championship for a third consecutive year.
item.content:encoded:
Speaking to fijivillage news, Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Vice-President, Josua Qalo says Wainibuka Secondary School announced itself as one of the teams to watch after winning the Under-15 title in the Eastern Rally.

He says Vunimono High School also continued its rise by claiming the Under-17 title, while retaining the boys' championship for a third consecutive year.

Qalo says Mahatma Gandhi Memorial School was another standout performer after winning both the Under-14 and Under-19 titles in the Central Rally, while St Joseph's Secondary School claimed the Under-17 title and Suva Grammar School won the Under-15 grade.

Despite the emergence of the new challengers, Adi Cakobau School showed it remains one of the competition's traditional powerhouses by defending both the Under-19 and Open grade titles in the Eastern Rally, while also finishing runners-up in the Under-15 and Under-17 grades.

Qalo says the Fiji Secondary Schools Netball Championships will be held in Suva on the 19th, 20th and 25th of August.

He says schools that qualified through the Eastern, Central, Northern, West One and West Two rallies will be joined by the winners of the Maritime Rally on the 17th of August.

Schools from the Lau Group, Lomaiviti and Kadavu will compete in the Maritime Rally for the remaining places in the national championships.

item.title: Rainibogi returns home to warm welcome after Commonwealth Games gold
item.description: Commonwealth Games gold medallist Taniela Rainibogi received a warm welcome at Nadi International Airport upon his return to Fiji following his historic victory in the men’s 110kg weightlifting event. Fiji Airports and Deputy Secretary for the Ministry of Youth and Sports, Philip Hereniko, were on hand to welcome the champion home and celebrate his achievement on the international stage.
item.content:encoded:
Commonwealth Games gold medallist Taniela Rainibogi received a warm welcome at Nadi International Airport upon his return to Fiji following his historic victory in the men’s 110kg weightlifting event.

Fiji Airports and Deputy Secretary for the Ministry of Youth and Sports, Philip Hereniko, were on hand to welcome the champion home and celebrate his achievement on the international stage.

Rainibogi’s gold medal win is a proud moment for the country, highlighting his dedication and hard work.

The Ministry of Youth and Sports says although Fiji is a small nation, its athletes continue to prove that determination and excellence know no boundaries.

The Ministry adds that Fiji’s success is a powerful reminder that the country can compete with the world’s best and achieve greatness through perseverance, talent and unity.

They have also congratulated the Fiji Weightlifting Team for its outstanding performance.

Meanwhile, Fiji finished 20th at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with one gold and one bronze medal through boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama.

item.title: Springbok Women brace for physical and unpredictable Fijiana challenge in historic Suva Test
item.description: The Springbok Women expect a physical and unpredictable challenge from the Vodafone Fijiana XV when the two sides meet in a historic Test match at 2pm this Saturday at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva. Springbok Women vice-captain and flyhalf Libbie Janse van Rensburg says her side knows what to expect from Fiji and are ready to match the Fijiana's physical style of play.
item.content:encoded:
The Springbok Women expect a physical and unpredictable challenge from the Vodafone Fijiana XV when the two sides meet in a historic Test match at 2pm this Saturday at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva.

Springbok Women vice-captain and flyhalf Libbie Janse van Rensburg says her side knows what to expect from Fiji and are ready to match the Fijiana's physical style of play.

Janse van Rensburg says Fiji is an unpredictable team that will be in their faces throughout the match, but South Africa will not shy away from the challenge.

She says the squad has now switched into Test mode after recovering from a two-day journey to Fiji and adjusting to the 10-hour time difference.

Janse van Rensburg says while this is the longest trip the team has made for a Test match, it is all part of their preparations for the remainder of the season and the lead-up to the 2028 Women's Rugby World Cup in Australia.

She says the absence of some experienced players, who remained in South Africa as part of a conditioning programme, has created an opportunity for other players to prove they deserve a regular place in the squad while also testing the team's depth.

The experienced playmaker, who is set to earn her 33rd Test cap, says she hopes to use her experience to guide the team, control the game at flyhalf and ensure the players stick to their game plan.

Janse van Rensburg also highlighted the breakdown as a key area South Africa must improve after it proved costly in their recent defeat to the USA, saying they will need to be much better in that area if they want to beat Fiji.

The Springbok Women's match-day squad for Saturday's Test will be announced tomorrow.

item.title: Tailevu rugby looking to build momentum
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 03/08/2026 Tailevu rugby captain Eparama Sailo says his side made a good start in the 2026 Skipper Cup Competition, but they now need to maintain that momentum throughout the season.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 03/08/2026

Tailevu rugby captain Eparama Sailo says his side made a good start in the 2026 Skipper Cup Competition, but they now need to maintain that momentum throughout the season.

Tailevu opened their 2026 Skipper Cup campaign with a 27-26 win over Navosa at Vatureba Park in Keiyasi.

Sailo says they expected a physical and tough contest against Navosa and is thankful to his players for putting in a full 80-minute performance.

He adds that his message to the team has been that great things can be achieved when they work together.

Tailevu will take on Ba this Saturday at 4R Stadium at Govind Park.

In other matches this week, Rewa will face Malolo, Navosa will host Taveuni at Vatureba Park in Keiyasi, Naitasiri will meet Kadavu at Ratu Cakobau Park, Lautoka will host Nadi at Churchill Park, and Nadroga will take on Suva at Lawaqa Park.

item.title: Springbok Women hold first Fiji training at Albert Park for Fijiana clash
item.description: Navitalai Naivalurua · 03/08/2026 The Springbok Women's XV held their first training session this morning at Albert Park in Suva as they prepare for their two-Test series against the Vodafone Fijiana XV.
item.content:encoded:
Navitalai Naivalurua · 03/08/2026

The Springbok Women's XV held their first training session this morning at Albert Park in Suva as they prepare for their two-Test series against the Vodafone Fijiana XV.

This marks the first time the South African women's team has toured Fiji.

The two teams have met once before, at the 2022 Women's Rugby World Cup in New Zealand, where Fiji claimed a 21-17 victory.

The Test matches are part of a short tour aimed at building experience and providing quality competition for both sides.

Team manager Thandiswa Nxomani says the tour is an important opportunity for the Springbok Women to push themselves outside their comfort zone by adapting to different conditions and time zones, which will be valuable preparation ahead of the Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Nxomani says Fiji will be a formidable opponent, especially after the Fijiana's recent appearance in the Super W Grand Final.

She adds that South Africa is well aware of the exciting brand of rugby Fiji plays and the challenge of overcoming the hosts on home soil.

According to World Rugby ranking, South Africa is on 10th place while Fiji is sitting on 13th place.

The Springbok Women will take on the Fijiana at 2pm at the HFC Bank Stadium this Saturday, with the second Test scheduled for 1pm at Churchill Park, Lautoka, next Saturday.

item.title: Fijiana ready for biggest physical test against South Africa this Saturday - Legge
item.description: The Vodafone Fijiana XV have turned their attention to winning collisions as preparations intensify for Saturday's Test against South Africa. Head coach Mike Legge says the team's first training session at Buckhurst Park today is primarily about getting the players back on the field after an eight-day break following the Super Rugby Women's season.
item.content:encoded:
The Vodafone Fijiana XV have turned their attention to winning collisions as preparations intensify for Saturday's Test against South Africa.

Head coach Mike Legge says the team's first training session at Buckhurst Park today is primarily about getting the players back on the field after an eight-day break following the Super Rugby Women's season.

Legge says the biggest lesson from Drua Women's Super Rugby Women's final defeat to the NSW Waratahs was the importance of dominating the physical contest.

He says he expects South Africa to present one of the toughest physical challenges the team has faced.

Insert: Legge - South Africa is a big team July 03

Legge says the South Africans arrive in Fiji in good form after a recent Test series against the United States and are continuing to improve.

He says they are in the top 10 for a reason, and will be a physical side that will test them.

While the contact area will be a major focus throughout the week, Legge says the team would remain committed to its attacking style of rugby.

The remaining members of the squad are also expected to join camp as preparations continue for Saturday's Test against South Africa.

The Fijiana's first Test against the Springboks will be held at the HFC Bank Stadium this Saturday at 2pm, while their second Test will be held at Churchill Park in Lautoka next Saturday at 1pm.

item.title: Team Fiji ends Glasgow Commonwealth Games campaign in 20th place
item.description: Team Fiji has finished 20th at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, winning one gold medal through weightlifter Taniela Rainibogi and one bronze medal through boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama. They share the spot with the Bahamas and the Isle of Men.
item.content:encoded:
Team Fiji has finished 20th at the 2026 Glasgow Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, winning one gold medal through weightlifter Taniela Rainibogi and one bronze medal through boxer Jasmine Daunakamakama.

They share the spot with the Bahamas and the Isle of Men.

The other standout performer for Team Fiji was swimmer David Tolu Young who finished 6th in the 50 metres freestyle finals.

Young is the first Fijian swimmer to make the finals in swimming.

Meanwhile in last night's competitions, Team Fiji judoka, Gerard Takayawa won his round of 16 elimination match in the Men's +100kg division defeating Adam Hall of Northern Ireland 101-0.

Takayawa went down to Canadian John Bassong in the quarterfinals 100-0.

He also lost out to Gregor Miller of Scotland in the repechage.

Team Fiji Swimming and Basketball athletes were welcomed back by Assistant Minister for Youth and Sports Aliki Bia last night.

Meanwhile, Australia dominated the medal tally with 70 gold, 45 silver, and 56 bronze, England is second with 29 gold, 45 silver, 36 bronze, while Canada scooped third with 19 gold, 20 silver and 23 bronze medals.
